title: The end of the track
text: Caliente was the end of the railroad for about sixteen months in the 1870s, while crews cut a line up over Tehachapi Pass. A force of up to three thousand men, most of them Chinese, did the heavy work on the mountain above the town.

s1.title: #0757 Caliente, California State Historical Landmarks
s1.quote: Originally known as Allen's Camp after Gabriel Allen, who in the 1870s had a cabin and stock pasture near here, the settlement was named Caliente when railroad construction reached this point in April 1875. The town became a railroad terminal for about 16 months while a force of up to three thousand men, most of them Chinese, labored on the heavy railroad construction on the mountain.

s2.title: Tehachapi Pass Railroad Line, National Historic Civil Engineering Landmark
s2.quote: The Tehachapi Pass Railroad Line was cut through solid and decomposed granite by about 3,000 Chinese laborers using nothing more than picks, shovels, horse drawn carts, and blasting powder.
